query: Why are some incidents resolved inefficiently, and which underlying issues drive it?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents by hardware/software domain gives a strong grouping axis for finding which issue types drive inefficient resolution. Values in samples are sound readings of the short_description (printer->printer_hardware, database->database).

per_column.name: issue_subtype
per_column.rationale: Finer-grained failure mode adds real analytical leverage beyond category. Mostly well grounded, though 'malfunction_generic' dominates and 'not_responding' vs 'malfunction_generic' for near-identical 'Printer not working' texts shows some inconsistent inference, mildly weakening groundedness.

per_column.name: affected_asset_type
per_column.rationale: Useful for asset-level analysis but heavily overlaps incident_category (printer_hardware/printer, database/database), reducing incremental leverage. Values are well grounded in the descriptions.

per_column.name: reassignment_flag
per_column.rationale: Reassignment is directly relevant to resolution inefficiency, a strong analytical axis. However the short_description/timestamps do not encode reassignment history; the true/false values appear inferred without textual support and are not derivable from the shown source fields.

per_column.name: requires_physical_intervention
per_column.rationale: Physical intervention plausibly correlates with slower resolution, giving useful grouping. Mostly a warranted inference from asset/issue type, though it is a derived judgment rather than stated fact, introducing some uncertainty.

per_column.name: resolution_action_type
per_column.rationale: Resolution action is highly relevant to the efficiency query. But the source text describes the problem, not the resolution taken; assigning specific actions like 'repair'/'replacement' is largely inferred and asserts specifics the text does not confirm.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Recurrence is a compelling driver of inefficiency and would be valuable. Yet nothing in the provided source text signals recurrence; the 160 true values appear invented, contradicting the silence of the text.

per_column.name: software_trigger_present
per_column.rationale: A software-vs-hardware trigger flag adds a modest axis but is largely derivable from category, so partially redundant. Values track description content reasonably.

per_column.name: urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: Urgency categorization is useful and partly redundant with existing priority column, but the multi-level signal from wording ('lost', 'unable') adds nuance. Inference from tone words is somewhat subjective but generally warranted.

judge.rationale: Most columns provide genuine grouping/modeling axes for diagnosing inefficient resolution (category, subtype, reassignment, action type, recurrence, urgency), with only affected_asset_type and software_trigger_present being partly redundant. The main weakness is groundedness: several high-value columns (reassignment_flag, resolution_action_type, recurrence_signal) assert specifics the problem-only source text cannot support, indicating invented rather than extracted values.
